text.p: The "general discharge" which Air Force Lt. Kelly Flinn accepted on Thursday to avoid a court martial does not carry the stamp of high approval that goes with an "honorable discharge," service officials said.

Although Flinn will receive a "general discharge under honourable conditions," the definition of that document suggests that all did not go well with her in the service, one official, who asked not to be identified, told reporters.
"Under honourable conditions, a general discharge is separation from the Air Force with honour, but to a lesser degree than an honourable discharge," said the official.
"This (general) discharge is given when normally faithful service is marred by negative aspects of a person's duty performance or personal conduct."

But Flinn -- who was accused of adultery, fraternisation, lying to investigators and disobeying an order -- did avoid the possibility of being ejected from the service under "other than honourable circumstances" and perhaps jailed had she been convicted in a court martial, officials said.
